name: image-picker
title: Image picker
description: Choose one image from a set of thumbnails, such as a cover, a header or a theme, as a radio group with a ring and a check on the pick; or several, up to a limit.
docs: images are { id, src, alt, label }. value and onValueChange speak the id (null when the choice is cleared), so what is stored never depends on an address. allowNone adds a first tile that clears the choice. With multiple, value is an array of ids and max stops the choice: the other tiles dim, the count under the grid says so, and a polite message explains it when someone tries; allowNone does not apply. columns (2 to 6) is the number of tiles in a row once the container has room: it follows container queries, so a narrow sidebar gets fewer whatever the screen, and aspect is width over height (16 / 10 by default, 1 for squares). It is a radio group (a group of checkboxes with multiple) with one tab stop: Tab goes to the chosen tile, the arrow keys move through the grid in two directions (Up and Down by a whole row as laid out right now), Home and End jump, Space or Enter chooses. A tile is named by its label, or by its alt text when it has no label, with Selected added when it is chosen, and the alt text describes it when there is a label. A picture that is loading shows the Skeleton, and one that fails falls back to a quiet block with its label. loading draws shaded tiles in place of the pictures, name posts the chosen id (one hidden input per id with multiple), noneLabel renames the first tile, and disabled turns it all off.
